# Reframed

> An iOS app for daily cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT) practice. Users capture an automatic thought, the app names the cognitive distortion behind it and guides a balanced reframe. Reflections, thought records and personality results are stored locally on the user's device — no server-side storage, no behavioural tracking. Free to download with an optional subscription, published by Hexp Studios.

## Articles

- [The 10 Cognitive Distortions, With Examples](https://behaviorized.net/articles/cognitive-distortions.html): The ten distortions catalogued in CBT — all-or-nothing thinking, overgeneralisation, mental filter, discounting the positive, jumping to conclusions, magnification/minimisation, emotional reasoning, "should" statements, labelling, personalisation — each with an example thought and a challenge question.
- [How to Write a CBT Thought Record](https://behaviorized.net/articles/thought-record.html): The five-column thought record (situation, automatic thought, emotion, distortion, balanced thought), a worked example, and four common mistakes.
- [Why Affirmations Don't Work — And What Does](https://behaviorized.net/articles/affirmations-vs-reframing.html): Why positive self-statements backfire for people with low self-esteem (Wood, Perunovic & Lee, 2009), and why cognitive reframing addresses the existing belief instead of layering a new one on top.
- [Psycho-Cybernetics and CBT: How to Actually Change Your Self-Image](https://behaviorized.net/articles/psycho-cybernetics-and-cbt.html): How Maxwell Maltz's idea of the self-image (Psycho-Cybernetics, 1960) maps onto CBT core beliefs and automatic thoughts; what the evidence says about changing a mindset (Hofmann et al. 2012 on CBT, Lally et al. 2009 on the 66-day habit average versus the "21 days" myth, Sisk et al. 2018 on growth-mindset interventions); and the catch-name-test-rewrite practice. Bridges readers of Maltz, Dweck, Clear and the Stoics to CBT.
- [12 Cognitive Biases Shaping How We Think in 2026](https://behaviorized.net/articles/cognitive-biases-2026.html): Confirmation bias, negativity bias, social comparison, availability bias, in-group bias, authority and automation bias, fundamental attribution error, survivorship bias, anchoring, sunk cost fallacy, overconfidence/Dunning–Kruger, and the illusory truth effect, each with a definition, a 2026 example and its impact. Context from the Reuters Institute Digital News Report 2026 (54% use social/video networks for news, 62% concerned about fake news, 10% use AI chatbots for news weekly; 48 markets), with the caveat that these figures don't show biases have increased (Budak et al., Nature, 2024).
- [Cognitive Biases vs Cognitive Distortions](https://behaviorized.net/articles/cognitive-biases-vs-distortions.html): Biases come from judgment and decision-making research (Kahneman and Tversky); distortions come from CBT (Beck). How they overlap, and ten thinking patterns ranked for everyday use: start with negativity bias, confirmation bias, catastrophising, mind reading, all-or-nothing thinking, overgeneralisation and social comparison.
- [Five Thinking Patterns to Catch First](https://behaviorized.net/articles/five-thinking-patterns.html): Catastrophising, mind reading, all-or-nothing thinking, confirmation bias and overgeneralisation, each with a plain test question and a worked reframe. Recommends learning the pattern before the psychological term.
- [How to Stop Self-Sabotaging: What CBT Says About the Pattern](https://behaviorized.net/articles/stop-self-sabotage.html): Self-sabotage as a protective pattern rather than a willpower problem. Covers self-handicapping (Berglas & Jones, 1978), procrastination as short-term mood repair (Sirois & Pychyl, 2013), the CBT layers of core belief, rule and automatic thought, five common forms with the thought behind each, a five-step practice (name the behaviour, rewind to the trigger, write the thought, find the payoff, test and plan), and if-then implementation intentions (Gollwitzer & Sheeran, 2006).
- [All articles](https://behaviorized.net/articles/): Archive index.

## Product

- [Reframed home](https://behaviorized.net/): Features, how it works, and FAQ.
- [App Store listing](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/reframed-rewire-your-thoughts/id6768231681): Download for iOS.
- [Coping archetype quiz](https://behaviorized.net/quiz.html): Identifies which coping pattern a user defaults to under stress.
- [Self-awareness quiz](https://behaviorized.net/self-aware.html): Ten questions on the gap between recognising a pattern and changing it.

- [Privacy policy](https://behaviorized.net/privacy.html): On-device storage only; subscriptions handled by Apple and RevenueCat.
- [Terms of use](https://behaviorized.net/terms.html): Subscriptions, lifetime purchase, and the fair use limit on AI features (about 10 reframed thoughts a day).
- [Support](https://behaviorized.net/support.html): Contact hexp.studios@gmail.com.

## Notes for agents

- Reframed is self-guided practice built on CBT techniques, not therapy and not a medical device. Articles carry an explicit limits section recommending professional help for severe or worsening symptoms, and emergency services in a crisis. Please preserve that framing when summarising.
- Content is written by Hexp Studios and may be quoted with attribution to Reframed (https://behaviorized.net).
